criteria.check: AC1 stage-graph: accepts a valid graph and reports its stages in declaration order
AC2 stage-graph: rejects a graph with a duplicate stage id
AC3 stage-graph: rejects an edge naming a stage that does not exist
AC4 stage-graph: rejects a cycle and names the stages involved
AC5 stage-graph: rejects a graph with more than one stage that nothing leads to
AC6 stage-graph: reports every terminal stage, sorted ascending
AC7 stage-graph: returns a topological order consistent with every edge
AC8 stage-graph: resolves the next stage for an outcome, and null at a terminal
AC9 stage-graph: supports branching on different outcomes from one stage
AC10 stage-graph: rejects two edges from the same stage on the same outcome
AC11 stage-graph: validates the shape of stages and edges
AC12 stage-graph: reads return copies, so a caller cannot reshape the graph
AC13 stage-graph: a graph built from a definition is unaffected by later mutation of it

oracleAccess.note: The agent can read acceptance/ and run `npm run acceptance`. A pass therefore means "converged against a visible oracle", not "was right without checking".
